tasks.title: Repair a synthetic reverse-proxy upstream
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied synthetic snapshot. Create fix.conf and diagnosis.json. Repair the ledger_backend reverse-proxy fragment for the supplied connection-refused and upstream-timeout evidence, with bounded retry and forwarding semantics. diagnosis.json must identify the evidence-limited incident cause and changes. Do not invoke nginx, a network client, SSH, Docker, systemd, sudo, or any host path.

tasks.title: Repair synthetic unit restart and readiness semantics
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied synthetic unit, environment, and event snapshots. Create service-fixed.unit and diagnosis.json with restart, dependency, environment, and file-based readiness semantics. The unit is data for a project-owned parser; do not run systemd or any real service command. Keep every referenced path within the task workspace and state only evidence-limited conclusions.

tasks.title: Correct a synthetic log-rotation policy
tasks.instruction: From the supplied synthetic retention incident, create logrotate-fixed.conf and diagnosis.json. Use a bounded weekly policy with safe ownership, compression, delayed compression, retention, and a project-local reload hook that preserves failure status. Do not run logrotate, reload a daemon, or use host paths.

tasks.title: Repair a synthetic backup schedule
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied schedule and failure snapshot. Create backup-fixed.sh and schedule.txt. The script must use UTC, a project-local lock, project-local snapshot and retention helpers, and failure propagation; the schedule must run it at 02:17 UTC. Do not run cron, use sudo, access host paths, or contact a service.

tasks.title: Prepare a synthetic TLS-chain deployment plan
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied certificate metadata. Create deployment.json and rollback.md for the supplied synthetic edge endpoint. Assemble leaf then issuing intermediate, exclude the root, use only task-local paths, record a local verification step, and describe bounded rollback. Do not use certificate tools, network tools, daemon commands, or host paths.

tasks.title: Triage synthetic disk and inode pressure
tasks.instruction: Correlate the supplied synthetic capacity snapshots. Create triage.json and remediation.md that identify block, inode, and deleted-open-file pressure, keep remediation bounded to supplied project paths, protect the current data path, and state evidence limits. Do not inspect the host filesystem or run destructive commands.

tasks.title: Bound a synthetic cgroup OOM incident
tasks.instruction: Use the supplied synthetic cgroup event and unit snapshot. Create service-fixed.unit and diagnosis.json that bound service memory, disable swap for the synthetic unit, use restart backoff, preserve project-local execution and readiness paths, and avoid unsupported certainty claims. Do not inspect cgroups or run systemd.

tasks.title: Repair synthetic proxy health semantics
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied synthetic proxy trace. Create proxy-fixed.conf and diagnosis.json with both supplied upstream members, bounded health, connect/read timeouts, forwarding headers, and retry semantics. The fragment is parser input only. Do not invoke a proxy, reach a port, or claim the incident is fully resolved.

tasks.title: Produce a bounded synthetic database-pool tuning plan
tasks.instruction: Correlate the supplied synthetic request, pool, and database metrics. Create tuning.json and rollback.md with the bounded pool settings, statement timeout, observation guardrails, and reversible rollback conditions. Do not connect to a database, inspect a host, or claim capacity has been proven.

tasks.title: Implement a synthetic atomic release rollback
tasks.instruction: Use only the supplied release snapshot. Create rollback.sh and rollback-plan.json. The shell artifact must validate a task-local release target, precheck its marker, atomically replace the task-local current symlink, verify through the supplied helper, restore the captured target on verification failure, and atomically write a local audit record. Do not execute the script against a host, invoke a service manager, or use absolute or parent paths.
